user_request: Fix the .md itself. Search online for best practices for starting sections, paragraphs and sentences and ending them. Review Paper 1. Section 2.2 must explain what short-time spectral estimation is, why needed and what the section will do. A bare degradation statement does not orient the reader.

sources.title: MIT Communication Lab: Journal Article Methods
sources.findings: Methods should explain why the methodology was chosen as well as allow replication. The purpose and application of the method matter, not merely the sequence of operations. Adjust explanatory depth to the intended specialists. Retain essential detail. This page favors focusing on methods rather than authors, including passive voice where appropriate. It does not prescribe one opening template.

sources.title: Harvard Writing Center: Anatomy of a Body Paragraph
sources.findings: A topic sentence establishes the main point and its connection to the larger argument. Develop it with evidence and interpretation. End with what the reader can now understand rather than a redundant summary or unsupported new idea. This is academic-essay guidance, so its rhetorical principles can inform engineering prose but its claim-evidence-analysis template is not mandatory for method derivations.

sources.title: Harvard Writing Center: Transitions
sources.findings: Transitions show relationships between ideas and their role in the argument. Familiar information can lead into new information. Identify the actual logical relation before choosing a connective. Adding therefore does not create a causal connection.

sources.title: Gopen and Swan: The Science of Scientific Writing (1990), primary article reprint
sources.findings: Readers use structure to interpret scientific meaning. Familiar context near a sentence beginning helps readers interpret new information. A sentence ending tends to receive emphasis, so place the intended new point there when natural. These are principles of reader expectations rather than universal rules for every sentence.

constraints: Replace or reorganize existing advice rather than adding a large checklist. Keep a concise general guide. No manuscript length target. Section openings have different jobs from middle sentences. Preserve passive voice, few commas, no semicolons or whose.

No universal ban on direct statements. Do not require This section or To openings, a recap, a summary, or an extra lead-in in every paragraph. A method subsection may explain its method through its role and operation rather than a dictionary definition. A short orientation can briefly recall established context without recapping the whole motivation. Promise only what the section delivers.

Root cause: the engineering-cause example in writing.md uses the same degradation line copied into the section opening. Replace that exemplar with guidance distinguishing rationale from orientation. Resolve direct conflicts rather than layering instructions.

Actual v22 equations are authoritative. The NCF now uses separate H and lambda C. P=L/K=1 and the cap are no longer in section 2.1. Correct the stale context bullet in writing.md that claims P=L/K=1 while keeping other facts unchanged. Do not restore old equations or capped-margin claims.

Section 2.2 computes short-window transforms, auto/cross spectra and recursively averaged spectra on selected bins. Identification follows in 2.3. Transforms alone are neither the plant-response estimate nor the margin. The reader is an engineer unfamiliar with this implementation, not a novice to Fourier theory.

Paper 1 illustrates rhetorical structure, not a mandatory template. It contains active, imperative and wordy passages too. Its section 3.2 states a study purpose. Section 4 connects previous work to a new task. Paragraph 245 introduces a physical model before details. Do not import claims into Paper 2.
